title: The extends Keyword
summary: Master the exact syntax, compilation mechanics, member accessibility, and rules of the extends keyword in Java.
learningObjectives: Master the exact syntax of the extends keyword in Java class declarations
Understand which members are inherited: public and protected members vs package-private and private members
Identify compilation errors when attempting to inherit from final classes or multiple classes
Learn how the Java compiler links inherited method calls during compilation
expectedOutcomes: Ability to write error-free class extension statements in Java
Confidence in choosing appropriate access modifiers for extensible class members

activities.title: The Passport Renewal Analogy
activities.content:
When you renew an international passport, the government issues an 'extended' passport. It keeps your primary legal identity (name, citizenship, biometric ID) while adding new visa pages and enhanced digital security chips.

You do not change your biological identity; you extend it with additional capabilities. In Java, the `extends` keyword does exactly this: it takes the entire approved identity and capabilities of the superclass and extends it with new child capabilities.

activities.title: Syntax, Rules, and Member Accessibility Under extends
activities.content:
The `extends` keyword establishes a compile-time inheritance relationship between two classes.

### 1. Syntax:
```java
public class SubClass extends SuperClass {
    // Subclass additions
}
```

### 2. Member Inheritance Rules:
Not every member in the superclass is accessible by the subclass:
- **`public` members**: Inherited and accessible everywhere.
- **`protected` members**: Inherited and accessible by subclasses in any package, plus any class in the same package.
- **Package-private (default)**: Inherited only if the subclass is in the **same package**.
- **`private` members**: NOT directly accessible by the subclass! They exist in the object's heap memory, but can only be accessed through public/protected getters and setters.
- **Constructors**: **Constructors are NOT members and are NEVER inherited!** A subclass must invoke a parent constructor using `super()`.

### 3. Critical Compilation Rules:
- **Rule 1: Exactly One Superclass**: Java allows extending only ONE class (`class C extends A` is legal; `class C extends A, B` is a compile-time error).
- **Rule 2: Cannot Extend `final` Classes**: If a class is declared `final` (e.g. `java.lang.String`), attempting to extend it causes a compile-time error.
- **Rule 3: Cyclic Inheritance is Illegal**: `class A extends B` while `class B extends A` causes a compiler cycle error.

activities.title: Mastery Verification: The extends Keyword (10 Questions)

questions.question: Which Java keyword is used to establish inheritance between two classes?
options: implements
extends
inherits
subclasses
questions.explanation: The 'extends' keyword is used for class-to-class inheritance in Java.

questions.question: Can a Java class extend more than one class directly (e.g. 'class C extends A, B')?
options: Yes, Java supports multiple class inheritance
No, Java strictly prohibits multiple class inheritance
Yes, if all classes are in the same package
Yes, if all parent constructors have no arguments
questions.explanation: Java supports only single class inheritance. Extending multiple classes produces a compile-time syntax error.

questions.question: Are constructors inherited by a subclass when using the extends keyword?
options: Yes, constructors are inherited just like normal methods
No, constructors are not members of a class and are never inherited
Only default zero-argument constructors are inherited
Only public constructors are inherited
questions.explanation: Constructors are never inherited. A subclass must define its own constructors and explicitly or implicitly invoke a superclass constructor.

questions.question: What happens if you attempt to write 'class MyString extends String' in Java?
options: It compiles normally
Compile-time error because java.lang.String is declared final
Runtime NoSuchClassException
It compiles but causes JVM crashes
questions.explanation: java.lang.String is a final class. The compiler prohibits extending any final class.

questions.question: Which superclass members can a subclass in a DIFFERENT package access directly?
options: Only public members
public and protected members
public, protected, and default members
All members including private
questions.explanation: Subclasses in different packages can access public and protected members of their superclass.

questions.question: What happens if class A extends B, and class B extends A?
options: Infinite inheritance loop at runtime
Compile-time error: cyclic inheritance involving A and B
Both classes become static
It works if both have zero constructors
questions.explanation: Cyclic inheritance is detected and rejected by the Java compiler during the compilation phase.

questions.question: If a superclass has a private field 'int id', how can the subclass access or modify it?
options: By writing super.id directly
Through public or protected getter and setter methods provided by the superclass
By re-declaring private int id in the subclass
Subclasses cannot access private fields under any circumstances
questions.explanation: Encapsulation requires accessing private parent state through public or protected accessor methods.

questions.question: Which of the following class declarations is syntactically valid in Java?
options: class Dog : Animal { }
class Dog inherits Animal { }
class Dog extends Animal { }
class Dog extends Animal, Mammal { }
questions.explanation: 'class Dog extends Animal { }' is the correct Java syntax.

questions.question: Can a subclass be declared in a different package than its superclass?
options: No, parent and child must share the same package
Yes, provided the superclass is declared public
Yes, but only if all fields are public
Only in Java 17 and above
questions.explanation: A subclass can reside in any package as long as the superclass is public and visible.

questions.question: What is the primary role of the extends keyword from the compiler's perspective?
options: To copy byte code from parent class into child class .class file
To establish a subtyping relationship and resolve inherited member lookup during symbol resolution
To run the parent class in a separate garbage collector nursery
To optimize JIT inlining only
questions.explanation: The compiler establishes the subtyping hierarchy and resolves inherited methods and fields during symbol resolution.

interviewQA.question: What is the exact syntax and purpose of the extends keyword in Java?
interviewQA.answer: The 'extends' keyword is written in a class declaration (e.g. 'class Sub extends Super') to signify that Sub inherits state and behavior from Super. It establishes a formal subtyping hierarchy where Sub acquires all accessible parent members.

interviewQA.question: Why are constructors not inherited in Java?
interviewQA.answer: Constructors are specifically responsible for initializing the exact class in which they are declared. If constructors were inherited, a subclass could be instantiated with only the parent's initialization logic, leaving subclass-specific fields uninitialized and violating object integrity.

interviewQA.question: What happens when a subclass declares a field with the exact same name as a field in its superclass?
interviewQA.answer: This is known as field shadowing (or field hiding). The subclass field does not override the parent field; both exist in the object. Within the subclass, the name refers to the child's field, while 'super.fieldName' can be used to refer to the parent's field.

interviewQA.question: Why does the Java compiler disallow extending final classes?
interviewQA.answer: Marking a class final is a deliberate architectural and security choice. It guarantees that the class implementation cannot be altered or subclassed by external developers, which is crucial for immutable classes like String and security-sensitive classes like System.

interviewQA.question: Explain member visibility for a subclass located in a different package from its superclass.
interviewQA.answer: The subclass can access public members and protected members. It cannot access package-private (default) members or private members of the superclass.

interviewQA.question: Can an abstract class extend a concrete class using the extends keyword?
interviewQA.answer: Yes. In Java, an abstract class can extend a concrete class, an abstract class can extend another abstract class, and a concrete class can extend an abstract class.

practiceProblems.title: Code from Scratch: Bank Account with Safe Private Access
practiceProblems.description: Demonstrate safe private access by building an Account parent with private pin and Savings child class.
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Build Account with private pin (String), protected balance (double), and a public method validatePin(String attempt). Then build SavingsAccount extending Account with interestRate (double) and applyInterest(String pinAttempt). From scratch.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Interest applied: $50.0. New balance: $1050.0
Invalid PIN attempt! Interest application rejected.
hints: In Account, pin is private, so SavingsAccount must call validatePin(attempt).
If validatePin returns true, add balance * (interestRate / 100.0) to balance.
If validatePin returns false, print the rejection error.

practiceProblems.title: Code from Scratch: Vehicle and Truck with Payload Limit
practiceProblems.description: Construct Vehicle base class and Truck subclass with max payload capacity enforcement.
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Create Vehicle with vin (String) and tareWeightKg (double). Subclass Truck adds maxPayloadKg (double) and currentCargoKg (double). Add loadCargo(double weightKg) that validates weight does not exceed maxPayloadKg.
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Loaded 3000.0 kg cargo on VIN-TRK-01
Rejected! 6000.0 kg exceeds remaining capacity of 2000.0 kg
hints: Vehicle constructor initializes vin and tareWeightKg.
Truck constructor passes vin and tareWeight to super().

practiceProblems.title: Fix Broken Code: Attempted Inheritance from Final Class
practiceProblems.description: Fix a compile error caused by attempting to extend a final class.
practiceProblems.problemStatement: The code fails to compile because EncryptedKey is marked final. Refactor the architecture so Key is a normal class that is extended, while EncryptedKey remains final as the leaf.
hints: Create class BaseKey with protected String keyHash.
Make CustomKey extend BaseKey instead of EncryptedKey.
Keep final on leaf classes if appropriate.

practiceProblems.title: Challenge: Multi-Attribute Sensor Extension
practiceProblems.description: Build an IoT Sensor hierarchy with telemetry polling and alert threshold checks.
practiceProblems.problemStatement: Create Sensor with sensorId (String), location (String), lastReading (double). Create TemperatureSensor extending Sensor with alertThresholdCelsius (double) and isAlertTriggered() returning lastReading > alertThresholdCelsius. Include recordReading(double value).
practiceProblems.expectedOutput:
Sensor S-101 [Server Room] reading: 24.5 C (Normal)
ALERT! Sensor S-101 [Server Room] reading: 36.2 C exceeds threshold of 30.0 C
hints: In Sensor, store fields as protected.
TemperatureSensor constructor passes sensorId and location to super().
recordReading updates lastReading and checks threshold.
